extracted.intended_audience: employers, HR professionals, labor/employment lawyers, and regulated stakeholders affected by the FLSA EAP exemption
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedures for updating the Department of Labor's standard salary level and highly compensated employee (HCE) total annual compensation threshold (how often, by what method, what data, and what notice). Applies to implementation and compliance with the final rule's automatic update mechanism for the EAP exemption thresholds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial update timing and severability
rubrics_metrics.description: The initial update will occur on July 1, 2024 (using current earnings data applied to the 2019 rule methodologies) with a change in methodologies for the standard salary level and HCE total annual compensation effective January 1, 2025; the Department intends the initial update to be severable from future triennial updates and from the methodology revisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The initial update will take effect approximately 60 days after publication of the final rule; notice procedures in §541.607(b)(3) will not apply to the initial update. The Department intends the initial update to remain in force even if later methodology changes or future triennial updates are stayed or do not take effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory authority to adopt an updating mechanism
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department grounds its authority to establish a mechanism for automatically updating the earnings thresholds in section 13(a)(1) of the FLSA, which gives the Secretary broad authority to define and delimit the scope of the EAP exemption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department may use notice-and-comment rulemaking to establish the methodology and the updating mechanism; once established by regulation, future updates apply current data to that pre‑established standard and do not themselves require separate notice-and-comment rulemaking. The updating mechanism does not preclude future rulemaking to change the methodology or the mechanism itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose: keep thresholds current to preserve exemption screening function
rubrics_metrics.description: Earnings thresholds must be kept up to date because, left unchanged, they become substantially less effective in helping identify exempt EAP employees as wages increase over time; regular updates ensure the thresholds remain effective and help define and delimit the EAP exemption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The updating mechanism is intended to prevent erosion of the thresholds' real value over time, provide predictability, and maintain the thresholds' utility in tandem with duties tests. The Department also intends the methodology changes to restore the salary level's historic screening function and to ensure the HCE threshold excludes all but employees 'at the very top of [the] economic ladder.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Update frequency — triennial updates (every 3 years)
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rule adopts an updating frequency of 3 years to reset the standard salary level and the HCE total compensation threshold.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department considered alternatives (annual, 4–6 years) and balanced keeping thresholds current against administrative burden on employers; triennial updates are judged frequent enough to maintain effectiveness without being overly burdensome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Updating methodology — fixed percentile approach using established methodologies
rubrics_metrics.description: Future updates will apply the same methodology used to set the thresholds (a fixed-percentile approach) so that the thresholds remain at the percentiles established through rulemaking rather than indexing to inflation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department rejected inflation-indexing alternatives and the asserted 'ratcheting' concern as unsubstantiated. Using a fixed percentile preserves the underlying salary-setting standard (maintains, rather than strengthens or weakens, the standard) and avoids deviations that indexing could introduce.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific percentiles for resetting thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: Absent further rulemaking, the second triennial update will reset the standard salary level to the 35th percentile of weekly earnings of full-time workers in the lowest-wage Census Region and will reset the HCE total annual compensation threshold to the annualized weekly earnings of the 85th percentile of full-time salaried workers nationally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These percentiles are the regulatory targets that the updating mechanism will preserve when applied to contemporaneous BLS data for future updates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data to use for updates — most recent available 4 quarters of BLS data
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department will update both thresholds using the most recent available four quarters of data, as published by the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS), preceding the publication of the Department's notice with the adjusted levels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters proposed alternatives (most recent quarter, six quarters, older quarters), but the Department concluded four quarters best balances reflecting prevailing conditions and commenters' concerns about longer/shorter data windows. Stakeholders can track the underlying BLS data quarterly to anticipate updates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and publication requirements prior to an update
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department will publish a notice in the Federal Register with the adjusted standard salary level and the HCE total annual compensation threshold at least 150 days before the date the adjusted thresholds are set to take effect, and will publish the updated thresholds on WHD's website no later than their effective date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A 150-day notice period was chosen to provide sufficient time for employers to prepare while allowing reliance on up-to-date data; some commenters sought longer notice, but the Department found longer periods would impair use of current data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pause mechanism for future updates
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department adopted a mechanism for pausing future updates to mitigate concerns that automatic updates could occur at inopportune times (e.g., during economic downturns).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The pause mechanism is intended to guard against undue increases during recessions or other adverse conditions; the preamble indicates this mechanism is a feature of the final rule, though detailed operational specifics are addressed elsewhere in the rule text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employer option to make a single adjustment covering multiple changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Because the initial update (July 1, 2024) and the subsequent change to the standard salary level and HCE methodology (January 1, 2025) are set forth in the final rule, some employers may choose to make a single adjustment at the first date that encompasses both the initial update and the impending change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an administrative/operational option employers may adopt to align budgeting and classification changes within a single adjustment rather than making separate changes within a 12‑month period.
